The Osun State Commissioner for Education, Professor Amare Omakasun, has urged candidates preparing for the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) to shun examination malpractice and embrace hard work, honesty and transparency. Omakasun gave the advice while speaking in a message to prospective candidates in a video posted on the Joint Admission and Matriculation Board’s (JAMB’s) X handle on Wednesday, warning that examination malpractice and attempts to cut corners could have serious consequences. He stressed that candidates should approach the examination with the understanding that gaining admission into higher institutions was not a do-or-die affair. “Examination is not a do-or-die affair. What we expect from you is complete transparency. If you cut corners, there are consequences,” he said. The commissioner advised candidates to study diligently and remain focused on their preferred courses, noting that adequate preparation was the best way to secure admission. He recalled that candidates had limited access to guidance during registration and had to complete their examination forms with little assistance. According to him, candidates in those days also had to wait for their results to be delivered to their post office after writing the examination. The commissioner disclosed that he scored 277 in his first UTME, using his experience to encourage prospective candidates to remain committed to their academic goals. He reiterated the need for candidates to avoid examination malpractice and concentrate on legitimate efforts to achieve success in the 2027 UTME.
